statusDefinitions.done: Acceptance evidence exists and the stated verification gate passed.
statusDefinitions.implemented-uncompiled: Code is present and static/smoke checks pass, but Rust compilation or real-provider execution is still missing.
statusDefinitions.blocked: Cannot be completed in the current environment or depends on an external prerequisite.
statusDefinitions.deferred: Intentionally postponed because the cost/risk is currently greater than the value.

tasks.title: Freeze fork baseline and preserve assets
acceptance: Original fork remains available as behavior reference
All 35 shipped image assets are byte-identical in the Tauri tree
tasks.nextAction: Use the immutable fork/tag and byte-pinned data fixtures as the rollback/reference source; do not restore a second runtime inside this tree.

tasks.title: Cross-check provider protocols against maintained official documentation
acceptance: Claude, CodeWhale, Codex, OpenCode and Aider contracts are recorded separately
Unsupported symmetry assumptions are explicitly rejected
tasks.nextAction: Re-run the scheduled drift gate whenever a provider CLI or Tauri/GitHub action contract changes.

tasks.title: Compile and type-check all Rust targets on Linux, Windows and macOS
acceptance: cargo check --all-targets passes on all three operating systems
Both native binaries build in release mode
blockedBy: Rust/Cargo are absent and the build container cannot resolve external hosts
Windows and macOS compilation require their native runners
tasks.nextAction: Run Tauri CI with the committed lock on Linux, Windows and macOS; fix compiler errors before treating any Rust path as verified.

tasks.title: Commit a resolved Cargo.lock
acceptance: Cargo.lock is produced by a successful supported-platform build
CI and release builds use --locked
tasks.nextAction: Validate the committed src-tauri/Cargo.lock through the three-platform --locked CI and retain the successful run as acceptance evidence.

tasks.title: Real GUI launch smoke on three platforms
acceptance: Transparent pet window appears
Tray menu opens
Details panel opens
App exits without orphan processes
blockedBy: No desktop session is available in the current container
Compiled platform binaries do not exist until P0-003/P0-004 pass
tasks.nextAction: Run the self-hosted real desktop workflow on Linux, Windows and macOS and retain screenshots plus clean-exit/orphan-process evidence.

tasks.title: Pin and monitor fork/provider protocol drift
acceptance: The source fork revision and tested CLI versions are recorded in every release candidate
Changes to provider, hook, metering and installer files reopen the relevant protocol gates
Drift detection never auto-merges upstream behavior into the Rust adapter
tasks.nextAction: Run the weekly remote contract job and opt-in real-provider gate; detected drift remains review-required and is never auto-merged.

tasks.title: Introduce provider capability/status model and renderer contract
acceptance: Renderer receives active/all/statuses/capabilities
Provider enable/disable triggers immediate resynchronization
tasks.nextAction: Confirm serialization and UI rendering in a compiled desktop build.

tasks.title: Claude merge-safe lifecycle and permission hooks
acceptance: Unrelated user hooks remain intact
PreToolUse emits current hookSpecificOutput schema
PermissionRequest can use the local approval service
tasks.nextAction: Compile, then verify Claude PreToolUse AskUserQuestion/ExitPlanMode updatedInput and PermissionRequest updatedPermissions against a current real CLI.

tasks.title: CodeWhale first-class TOML hooks with fail-safe ask
acceptance: Current maintained lifecycle/subagent events are installed
tool_call_before runs foreground
Local service failure returns explicit ask instead of empty stdout
tasks.nextAction: Validate with the exact CodeWhale fork CLI, including Standard and Full Access modes.

tasks.title: Codex hooks.json integration and trust-review status
acceptance: Nested hooks.json schema is used
PermissionRequest is blocking
UI tells the user to review with /hooks
Windows command path is shell-safe
tasks.nextAction: Compile and run /hooks trust review; verify Codex allow/deny envelopes remain minimal and never return reserved updatedInput/updatedPermissions.

tasks.title: OpenCode official ESM observation plugin
acceptance: Plugin exports an ESM plugin function
Lifecycle/tool events reach the local state endpoint
Permission events are observed but not externally overridden
tasks.nextAction: Run in OpenCode with plugin loading diagnostics and confirm event payload shapes.

tasks.title: Aider turn-completion notification bridge
acceptance: Canonical notifications-command key is used
Foreign user command is not overwritten
Only turn completion is promised
tasks.nextAction: Test notification stdin/arguments on current Aider versions across shells.

tasks.title: Provider install/uninstall idempotence and ownership boundaries
acceptance: Two installs produce no duplicate owned hooks
Uninstall removes only Octopus-owned entries
Malformed marker blocks fail without data loss
tasks.nextAction: Add Rust unit tests for malformed TOML/YAML markers and JSON hook group ownership.

tasks.title: Real-provider CLI contract suite
acceptance: Every installed provider emits at least session-start/tool/turn-end events as supported
Permission decisions are verified with allow/deny/ask
CLI version is recorded in evidence
blockedBy: Provider CLIs are not installed in the current container
Real credentials and interactive/native terminal contexts are external prerequisites
tasks.nextAction: Run the isolated self-hosted provider matrix with installed CLIs and record versions, redacted transcripts, events and native permission outcomes.

tasks.title: Provider-neutral usage event model with deduplication
acceptance: Usage events carry provider/model/session/turn identifiers and recorded price provenance
Duplicate hook delivery is idempotent across restart
Unknown field names are preserved for schema-drift diagnostics without persisting raw prompt or tool values
tasks.nextAction: Compile and execute the Rust ledger tests on all three OSes; retain JSONL unless measured concurrency or volume justifies SQLite.

tasks.title: CodeWhale turn_end token ingestion
acceptance: Input/output/cache hit/cache miss values are recorded
Totals reconcile with sample CodeWhale payloads
Missing usage fields do not corrupt prior totals
tasks.nextAction: Run the fixture and live CodeWhale turn_end payload through compiled binaries; reconcile token/cache/cost totals against CodeWhale scorecard output.

tasks.title: Claude transcript incremental scanner parity
acceptance: Only appended bytes are parsed
File truncation/rotation recovers safely
Legacy fork fixtures produce equivalent totals
tasks.nextAction: Compile and run the Rust scanner against anonymized real Claude transcripts on all three platforms; compare totals and truncation recovery with the fork reference fixtures.

tasks.title: Price catalog cache and historical pricing
acceptance: Bundled fallback prices work offline
Remote updates are signed or validated and cached atomically
Historical sessions retain the price version used
tasks.nextAction: Compile and exercise 200/304/timeout/offline flows on Linux, Windows and macOS; compare provider-qualified estimates with actual invoices before calling historical pricing verified.

tasks.title: Canonical session state machine and stale-event ordering
acceptance: Provider events map through one documented transition table
Late events cannot overwrite newer state
Session end expires cleanly
tasks.nextAction: Compile and replay out-of-order/duplicate lifecycle fixtures on all three platforms; verify sequence, timestamp, terminal-rank and 30-minute SessionEnd expiry behavior.

tasks.title: Reply bubble extraction with privacy limits
acceptance: Only the configured tail of assistant output is shown
Secrets/tool output are not surfaced by default
Bubble rendering is event-driven
tasks.nextAction: Compile and verify replyBubbles/replyBubbleChars on real Claude sessions, including secret-bearing, tool-result and long Unicode outputs.

tasks.title: Multi-provider concurrent-session UX
acceptance: Multiple active sessions are distinguishable
Aggregate pet state has deterministic precedence
Panel can filter by provider/session
tasks.nextAction: Compile and run concurrent Claude/CodeWhale/Codex sessions; verify deterministic active-state priority and provider/project/session filtering under live updates.

tasks.title: Provider-specific permission semantics without false equivalence
acceptance: Claude/CodeWhale/Codex each use their native decision contract
OpenCode and Aider remain honest about unsupported external steering
Full-access modes are displayed as bypassing ask where applicable
tasks.nextAction: Run real Claude, CodeWhale and trusted Codex permission prompts; verify byte-exact native envelopes and visible bypass/trust warnings. Confirm OpenCode/Aider remain native-only.

tasks.title: Approval queue durability, timeout and cancellation
acceptance: Pending prompts have provider/session/tool identity
Timeout resolves conservatively
App shutdown does not silently allow blocked actions
tasks.nextAction: Compile and stress exact-retry deduplication plus distinct parallel requests on all three operating systems; verify one resolved card never idles a session with another card pending.

tasks.title: Structured elicitation and plan-review parity
acceptance: Supported providers render structured options
Unsupported providers fall back to their native terminal UI
No fake success is shown
tasks.nextAction: Compile and run real Claude AskUserQuestion and ExitPlanMode flows; verify fallback to native terminal UI when the local service is unavailable.

tasks.title: Preserve parallel permission cards and exact-retry deduplication
acceptance: Distinct permission requests sharing one session remain separate cards
Only identical provider/session/tool/input retry connections share one decision
Resolving one card keeps the session waiting while another card remains
tasks.nextAction: Compile and execute concurrent real Claude permission requests, including parallel/background agents that share a session id.

tasks.title: Session process discovery and terminal focus abstraction
acceptance: macOS, Windows and X11 adapters are isolated
Wayland degradation is explicit
Focus never targets an unrelated terminal
tasks.nextAction: Compile and test source-PID ancestry focus on macOS, Windows and X11; record the explicit unsupported result on pure Wayland.

tasks.title: Territory/window-push feature by platform capability
acceptance: macOS/Windows/X11 implementations are permission-aware
Wayland reports unsupported instead of pretending success
Feature is isolated from core release readiness
tasks.nextAction: Resume only after core hooks, metering and focus parity pass.

tasks.title: Suspend/resume, display-change and multi-monitor recovery
acceptance: Pet returns to a visible monitor after topology change
No duplicate polling timers appear after resume
Window scale is stable on mixed DPI
tasks.nextAction: Run suspend/resume, monitor unplug/replug and mixed-DPI checks on each real desktop runner; verify only one 30-second health thread exists.

tasks.title: Idle CPU, RSS, startup and long-run benchmark
acceptance: Idle CPU <0.5% of one logical core in defined test conditions
Idle RSS target is measured per OS
8-hour growth and wakeups are recorded
Cold-start P50/P95 are reported
tasks.nextAction: Run 5-minute smoke and 8-hour release benchmarks on real desktop runners; publish raw CPU/RSS/startup/wakeup samples before accepting targets.

tasks.title: Asset delivery optimization with visual regression
acceptance: Original assets remain archived
Optimized copies are visually compared
Animation CPU/GPU cost is measured
tasks.nextAction: Capture compiled GUI pixel/animation snapshots per OS before converting any image; current active assets intentionally remain byte-identical originals.

tasks.title: Signed and reproducible Windows/macOS/Linux packages
acceptance: Windows package is signed
macOS package is signed and notarized
Linux packages run on the documented baseline
SBOM/checksums are published
tasks.nextAction: Provide protected updater, Windows and Apple signing/notarization secrets, commit Cargo.lock, run the release workflow and verify installed artifacts plus attestations.

tasks.title: Security review of local HTTP and hook command surface
acceptance: Loopback binding/token checks are fuzzed
Request sizes and timeouts are bounded
Command strings resist spaces and shell metacharacters
Sensitive payloads are redacted in logs
tasks.nextAction: Compile and fuzz the raw HTTP parser on all three OSes, verify generated pet/panel ACL permissions at runtime, then execute real shell/path-metacharacter provider tests.

tasks.title: Data-only fork behavior fixture pack
acceptance: Representative fork payload fixtures are anonymized and checked in independently of any retired runtime
Fixture hashes are pinned and verified by the active test chain
Known intentional differences are documented
tasks.nextAction: Add new fixtures only through explicit provider or upstream contract review.

tasks.title: Remove retired Electron/Node runtime from the source tree
acceptance: The source tree contains no archived Electron runtime, Chromium payload, main/preload/backend/provider Node runtime, or obsolete Node hook path
No active source or test imports an archived runtime
Rollback is external through immutable repository/tag archives rather than a second shipped runtime
tasks.nextAction: Keep package-content checks in the signed release gate; do not reintroduce a second runtime.
